| **Size** | The frame size, or **Custom…** with width and height fields on the row below. | The format's first row |
| **Frame rate** | **Project rate**, or a fixed rate. | Project rate |
| **Quality** | **Format default**, or a bit-rate tier. | Format default |
| **Loudness** | **Off**, a loudness target, or **Custom…** with a LUFS field. | Off |
| **Range** | **Whole project**, or **In/out range** when one is set. | Whole project |
| **Burn in timecode** | Draws the project timecode into the picture. | Off |

Under the controls, a readout line describes the file and a footnote names the codec, the container and the rates the file will use. Every number they show is the size, rate and duration the file will actually have.

- **Readout:** `1920 × 1080 · 30 fps · 00:01:12:05` (size, frame rate, duration). For the audio-only formats it reads `Audio only · 00:01:12.200`. For GIF and APNG it adds the frame count: `· 360 frames, no audio`. For **AV1 (MP4)**, **AV1 (WebM)**, **VP9 (WebM)** and **VP9 with Alpha (WebM)** a second line estimates how long the export will take: `Estimated time: about 25 s` (in 5-second steps under a minute, then minutes, then hours and minutes). It follows the format, Speed, size and range, and it is only an estimate: the figures behind it come from one measured export per format, so a busy Mac or a heavy timeline takes longer. The other formats show no estimate.
- **Footnote:** the codec, the container (left out when it is the same word, as in `GIF`), the AV1 speed (`AV1 · MP4 · Balanced`, `AV1 · WEBM · Balanced`; VP9 has none: `VP9 · WEBM`, `VP9 · WEBM · alpha`), the video rate, the audio rate (`192 kbps audio`), the loudness target (`−14 LUFS`) and `alpha` when the format keeps transparency. When you pick a Quality tier and the format sets its own rate, it reads `format's own rate` instead of a number.

A control the chosen format cannot use is greyed out rather than hidden. Its value is not sent.

### Format


The Size control is greyed out for the audio-only formats.

### Speed

The **Speed** row sits under Format (under Dynamic Range in an HDR project). It is live only on **AV1 (MP4)** and **AV1 (WebM)**; on every other format it is greyed out and keeps your last choice. **VP9 (WebM)** and **VP9 with Alpha (WebM)** have one speed, so the row is greyed out there too.

| Choice | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Faster** | The quickest AV1 export, a slightly larger file for the same picture. |
| **Balanced** | The default. |
| **Smaller file** | The slowest AV1 export, the smallest file for the same picture. |

AV1 and VP9 are encoded in software, so they take longer than the HEVC formats, which use the Mac's hardware encoder. The choice is remembered with the rest of the sheet and stored in presets.

### Frame rate

## The Export Queue

**Window ▸ Export Queue** lists queued exports. It opens on its own whenever you click **Add to Queue**.

- Jobs run **one at a time**, in the order they were added, while you keep editing.
- An **AV1** or **VP9** job also waits for memory. These formats are encoded in software and use a lot of it: about 1.2–2.3 GB at 1080p and 4.4–7.9 GB at 4K for AV1, depending on Speed, and about 0.4–0.5 GB at 1080p and 1.1–1.6 GB at 4K for VP9. All AV1 and VP9 exports running in Frame Job at once, from the queue and from **Export…** progress sheets, may use up to a quarter of the Mac's memory together. A queued AV1 or VP9 job that would go over waits until enough of them finish, and its row says why. The row's status is one line and ends in "…" where the sentence does not fit, which at most window widths is before the figures; hold the pointer over the row and its tooltip ends with the whole sentence: "Waiting for memory: AV1 and VP9 exports running now hold about 2.3 GB of the 4.0 GB this Mac allows them, and this one needs about 2.2 GB." While it waits, a later job that fits runs first. When nothing else is running, a job always starts, however large. An **Export…** sheet never waits: it is counted, and starts straight away.
- A job holds the timeline **as it was when you confirmed it**, including its media files, reversed clips and graphics. Edits, undos, relinks and even closing the document afterwards do not change what it writes.
- Each row shows the file's name and its state: **Waiting** (or the memory wait above), *Writing · 42 %* (or the measuring phase), the "Exported …" line with its loudness figures, **Cancelled.**, **Cancelled before it started.**, or the reason a job failed. The tooltip shows the full path, the format, size and frame rate, the whole memory-wait sentence while a job waits for memory, and any graphic warnings.
- **Cancel** on a row stops that job and removes its half-written file. On a finished row the button reads **Remove** and takes the row out of the list. **Show** reveals a finished file in the Finder.
- If a later export writes to the same file, the earlier finished row reads "Overwritten by a later export to the same file."
- WAV and AIFF are 16-bit only.
- On an M1 or M2 Mac Frame Job cannot play or re-import its own AV1 file, MP4 or WebM; QuickTime cannot either. Those Macs have no AV1 decoder. A VP9 (WebM) file re-imports on any Apple silicon Mac.
- AV1's and VP9's file size is not known in advance: the file usually comes in well under the rate, but very detailed footage can go up to about 1.25 times over it with AV1 and about 1.15 times with VP9.
- Captions are burned in, never a switchable subtitle track.
- Queued jobs run one at a time. **Export…** does not join the queue: it writes straight away, behind its own progress sheet.
- A queued AV1 or VP9 job waits while the AV1 and VP9 exports already running would use more than a quarter of the Mac's memory with it. The memory each needs is a measured figure, not a guarantee: a heavier timeline can use more. An **Export…** sheet is never held, so starting several AV1 or VP9 sheets at once can go past that quarter.
- The estimated time comes from one measured export per format on one Mac, and is provisional until it is measured on a quiet machine.
- Quitting during an **Export…** progress-sheet export does not ask and leaves a half-written file. Only the Export Queue is guarded at quit.

A queued AV1 or VP9 job that would go over waits until enough of them finish, and its row says why. The row's status is one line and ends in "…" where the sentence does not fit, which at most window widths is before the figures; hold the pointer over the row and its tooltip ends with the whole sentence: "Waiting for memory: AV1 and VP9 exports running now hold about 2.3 GB of the 4.0 GB this Mac allows them, and this one needs about 2.2 GB." While it waits, a later job that fits runs first. When nothing else is running, a job always starts, however large. An **Export…** sheet never waits: it is counted, and starts straight away.
- A job holds the timeline **as it was when you confirmed it**, including its media files, reversed clips and graphics. Edits, undos, relinks and even closing the document afterwards do not change what it writes.
- Each row shows the file's name and its state: **Waiting** (or the memory wait above), *Writing · 42 %* (or the measuring phase), the "Exported …" line with its loudness figures, **Cancelled.**, **Cancelled before it started.**, or the reason a job failed. The tooltip shows the full path, the format, size and frame rate, the whole memory-wait sentence while a job waits for memory, and any graphic warnings.
- **Cancel** on a row stops that job and removes its half-written file. On a finished row the button reads **Remove** and takes the row out of the list. **Show** reveals a finished file in the Finder.
- If a later export writes to the same file, the earlier finished row reads "Overwritten by a later export to the same file."
- WAV and AIFF are 16-bit only.
- On an M1 or M2 Mac Frame Job cannot play or re-import its own AV1 file, MP4 or WebM; QuickTime cannot either. Those Macs have no AV1 decoder. A VP9 (WebM) file re-imports on any Apple silicon Mac.
- AV1's and VP9's file size is not known in advance: the file usually comes in well under the rate, but very detailed footage can go up to about 1.25 times over it with AV1 and about 1.15 times with VP9.
- Captions are burned in, never a switchable subtitle track.
- Queued jobs run one at a time. **Export…** does not join the queue: it writes straight away, behind its own progress sheet.
- A queued AV1 or VP9 job waits while the AV1 and VP9 exports already running would use more than a quarter of the Mac's memory with it. The memory each needs is a measured figure, not a guarantee: a heavier timeline can use more. An **Export…** sheet is never held, so starting several AV1 or VP9 sheets at once can go past that quarter.
- The estimated time comes from one measured export per format on one Mac, and is provisional until it is measured on a quiet machine.
- Quitting during an **Export…** progress-sheet export does not ask and leaves a half-written file. Only the Export Queue is guarded at quit.

#!/bin/sh
# waits up to $1 seconds for 1-minute load <= 4; prints uptime; exit 0 if idle, 1 if not
end=$(( $(date +%s) + $1 ))
while :; do
  L=$(sysctl -n vm.loadavg | awk '{print $2}')
  if awk "BEGIN{exit !($L <= 4)}"; then uptime; exit 0; fi
  [ $(date +%s) -ge $end ] && { uptime; exit 1; }
  sleep 10
done
EOF

#!/bin/sh
# waits up to $1 seconds for 1-minute load <= 4; prints uptime; exit 0 if idle, 1 if not

  sleep 10
done

content.content:
## C6a — the Export Queue's memory limit and the sheet's estimate

### Record

**Decision.** CX-18, recorded before the code (`designs/spec/11-decisions/codec-export.md`;
amends #326's `queued` answer). The queue stays one job at a time; a bundled-encoder export
(settings with a `writer`) is booked in `ExportEncoderLedger` from just before its
`Exporter.export` call to its finish — the queue's running job and every Export… progress
sheet's; a queued encoder job is admitted when nothing is booked or the booked costs and its
own fit a quarter of physical memory; a held job is passed over by a later admitted one and
says why; a sheet is counted, never held; a writer row with no measured entry (C5's alpha row
until it is measured) costs the whole budget. No format bump, op or `rc_*`.

**What landed.**
- `app/Sources/ExportEncoderCosts.swift` (new): `ExportEncoderKey` (row, AV1 speed, bit
  depth), `ExportEncoderFigure` (1080p and 4K, proportional below 1080p, linear above),
  `ExportTimeEntry`, the `memory` and `time` tables with their sources, `memoryBytes`,
  `estimatedSeconds`, `estimateText` and `sheetLine`.
- `app/Sources/ExportEncoderLedger.swift` (new): the shared main-thread ledger, its
  notification, the budget (physical / 4), the admission rule, the held sentence, `begin`
  and `end`.
- `ExportQueueController.swift`: admission through the ledger with pass-over, each held
  job's `message`, the ledger observer re-running `start()`, `begin` before
  `exporter.export` in `launch`, and `finished` clearing its token before `end`.
- `ExportProgressSheetController.swift`: `begin` in `viewDidAppear` before `export`; `end`
  first in `finished` and in `deinit`, the token cleared first.
- `ExportQueueWindowController.swift`: `ExportQueueRowView.status(_:)` internal, `.waiting`
  reading `job.message ?? "Waiting"`.
- `ExportSheetResolve.swift`: the summary's second line (two lines added; 581).
- `ExportSheetController.swift`: the hint's queue sentence names the memory wait.
- `AgentServer+ExportStatus.swift`: `queued` adds `waiting`; `queued` and `running` add
  `estimated_seconds`. `AgentCatalog+Render.swift`: `export`'s and `export_status`'s text.
- Spec §7.4, §7.8, §7.9a; the guide's export page; `app/CLAUDE.md`'s map;
  `tools/proof/README.md`.

**The measurement** (`RC_PROOF_APP=release python3 tools/proof/encoder_memory_measure.py`,
2026-10-28, Release built from the tree before any C6a code, Apple M2 Max, 96 GiB; one fresh
instance per row; AV.mov twice, 10 s, 300 frames; Δ = peak − baseline RSS sampled every
0.1 s; seconds the done answer's `elapsed`; load the 1-minute average at the export's start).
**Taken on a shared machine**: the C5 lane (`~/devel/framejob-codecs`) was building and
running proofs at the same time, which is why the load rose from about 9 in the first half
to about 33 in the second. The JSON is `tools/proof/work/encoder-memory/2026-10-28/memory.json`
(gitignored). Every instance log was free of `Frame Job: ` lines.

| Key | Size | Δ RSS GiB | Δ bytes | Baseline GiB | Peak GiB | Seconds | s/frame | Load |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| av1 faster | 1920×1080 | 1.26 | 1,354,825,728 | 0.17 | 1.43 | 1.342 | 0.00447 | 10.47 |
| av1 balanced | 1920×1080 | 2.02 | 2,172,993,536 | 0.17 | 2.19 | 2.088 | 0.00696 | 9.79 |
| av1 smaller | 1920×1080 | 2.25 | 2,419,654,656 | 0.17 | 2.42 | 2.614 | 0.00871 | 9.72 |
| av1_webm faster | 1920×1080 | 1.24 | 1,331,265,536 | 0.17 | 1.41 | 1.296 | 0.00432 | 9.03 |
| av1_webm balanced | 1920×1080 | 2.01 | 2,158,755,840 | 0.17 | 2.18 | 2.038 | 0.00679 | 9.03 |
| av1_webm smaller | 1920×1080 | 2.22 | 2,378,907,648 | 0.17 | 2.38 | 2.661 | 0.00887 | 10.14 |
| vp9_webm SDR (8-bit) | 1920×1080 | 0.36 | 388,530,176 | 0.17 | 0.53 | 2.061 | 0.00687 | 10.21 |

| vp9_webm HLG (10-bit) | 3840×2160 | 1.58 | 1,694,040,064 | 0.23 | 1.81 | 9.078 | 0.03026 | 30.58 |
| h264 (control) | 3840×2160 | 0.25 | 271,679,488 | 0.17 | 0.42 | 3.284 | 0.01095 | 26.72 |

`ExportEncoderCosts.memory` is the Δ bytes column, transcribed exactly; `time`'s per-frame
seconds are each row's `seconds / 300`, `setupSeconds` 0. What the figures are and are not:
- The picture is AV.mov (640 × 360) scaled to the canvas, which is easy to encode: these
  speeds are far above the spike's `real8` (SVT preset 6 at about 75 fps at 1080p, here
  about 144 fps including the composition), and the per-frame time carries the
  composition, the loudness pass and the container besides the encoder. The memory is the
  encoder's lookahead and reference buffers at the size, which depend on the picture far
  less, and the 1080p AV1 figures sit beside the spike's 1,149–1,567 MB maximum RSS.
- One run each, the samples 13–81 per export (0.1 s apart); a peak between samples is
  missed, so a figure can be low by a sample's worth of growth.
- The 4K `smaller` rows were slower than `balanced` on `av1` (8.043 against 8.403 s) under
  very different loads (34.8 against 8.8): the time figures are PROVISIONAL, and C6b owes
  4K on every row and the idle three-run speeds that replace them.
- What the limit means on real Macs: a quarter of 32 GiB (8 GiB) admits one AV1 job at 4K
  at any speed, three at 1080p Balanced, and seven VP9 SDR jobs at 4K; on 16 GiB (4 GiB) one
  AV1 4K job always runs alone (CX-18 (5)) and nothing joins it. Since the queue runs one
  job at a time, the hold bites only beside Export… sheets.

**The probe needs no instance.** The spec had the probe open packages the proof saved over
MCP, so `--probe` would have needed an app; instead `encoder_limit_probe.swift` builds A1's
and W9's projects in process from AV.mov, as `webm_readers_probe.swift` builds A1's, and
`--probe` runs with no app at all. Q5's empty-project refusals use A1's `av1` settings over
an empty handle, because the core resolves no settings for an empty range.

**Proof** (2026-10-28, the same shared machine, load 30–100 from the C5 lane).
- `make gate`: PASS on the second attempt. The first stopped at `test` on
  `graphic/tests/path.rs`'s `a_path_over_the_memos_cost_bound_measures_the_same_twice` ("over
  the 250 ms budget at frame 7") with a load average near 100. No graphic file changed; the
  re-run passed `test` (155 s) and `app` (160 s), the earlier steps skipped as unchanged.
- `RC_PROOF_APP=release python3 tools/proof/encoder_limit_proof.py`: **17/17**.
  - Q1: the sheet (W9 as `av1` Smaller, 3,600 frames at 1080p) cost 2,419,654,656 bytes and
    the budget was set equal to it. A (`av1` Balanced, A1, 241,443,726) was held: "Waiting
    for memory: AV1 and VP9 exports running now hold about 2.3 GB of the 2.3 GB this Mac
    allows them, and this one needs about 0.2 GB." B ran and finished at sequence 5–61 and C
    at 62–136. The sheet finished at 137, A launched at 137 inside the sheet's `end`, and A
    finished at 147.
  - Q3, at 1 TiB: A was running at sequence 3 and the sheet finished at 13.
  - Q5: the ledger was empty at all five points.
  - S1 read "640 × 360 · 30 fps · 00:00:05:00\nEstimated time: about 5 s".
  - X1's `estimated_seconds` was 0, as the table gives: 150 frames at 640 × 360 come to
    about 0.12 s, and the sheet's floor is "about 5 s".
- The same proof against Debug: 17/17. `--probe`: 13/13.
- **Mutants** (`--mutant`, a probe over a copy of `app/Sources`): **10/10 caught**.

  | Mutant | Rows failing |
  |---|---|
  | no-hold | R1, Q1, and Q2, Q4, R2 besides |
  | strict-order | Q1, and Q4 |
  | sheet-uncounted | Q1, and Q2, Q4 |
  | no-wake | Q1 |
  | budget-half | R1, and Q1, Q2, Q4, R2 |
  | estimate-flat | E1, and R1, Q1, Q2, Q4 (the shared `value(pixels:)` moves the costs too) |
  | no-waiting-key | Q2 |
  | row-says-waiting | Q4 |
  | begin-late | Q5 |
  | token-overwrite | Q5 |

- `phase7_chrome.py`: 75/79. That is the same as the unchanged tree at `546df3f`, run on
  this machine the same day with C6a's changes stashed. Both runs fail the same four
  Document-pane translucent-canvas render checks; the queue's sections pass in both.
- `RC_PROOF_APP=release python3 tools/proof/export_status_proof.py`: 9/9.
- No instance log carried a `Frame Job: ` line.

**Owed (C6b).**
- 4K on every row.
- Idle three-run speed figures on a quiet machine.
- `ExportEncoderCosts.time` replaced by them, with `setupSeconds` separated from the
  per-frame time if the runs show one.

**Owed (C5).** `vp9_alpha_webm` has no memory entry, so it costs the whole budget (R2). Its
measured cost is one `memory` row (and one `time` row for an estimate) added through
`encoder_memory_measure.py`'s `KEYS`. **Paid** in C5's fix pass 1 ("## C5").

### Fix pass 1 (2026-10-28): the held sentence in the tooltip, the review's nits, two residues

**The should-fix: the held sentence was unreadable.** The queue row's status label is one
mono line that truncates its tail, so at the window's width the held sentence lost its GB
figures, and the tooltip did not carry them either. `ExportQueueRowView.toolTip(for:)` now
ends with `job.message` while the job waits, so the whole sentence is a hover away. The row
stays one line: its height is fixed (52 pt) and a wrapped status label in its stack would
need its own width solving, so wrapping was not taken. The guide's export page says what the
window shows: one line, cut with "…" where it does not fit, and the whole sentence in the
tooltip; spec §7.8 says the same.

**The nits, all fixed (the owner's residue rule).**
1. `ExportEncoderCosts.estimatedSeconds` answers nil when `sequenceFrameCount` is nil (a rate
   that cannot be stepped), so the sheet shows no estimate line and `export_status` has no
   `estimated_seconds`, where before it estimated 0 frames as "about 5 s" and 0. CX-18 (9)
   and §7.8 say so.
2. `encoder_memory_measure.py` fails a case whose baseline RSS cannot be read, instead of
   recording the whole peak as its delta.
3. `docs/manual-checks.md` SE-20: the sheet's estimate line on each AV1 and VP9 choice, and
   a held queue row and its tooltip, in both appearances.

**The proof.** Q4 also reads `toolTip(for:)`: A's ends with the whole sentence, and C's has
no "Waiting for memory" line. E3 also takes `av1` at fps 0/1 (no frame count): no line, no
seconds. Two mutants were added, one per new branch: `tip-drops-hold` (Q4) and
`estimate-no-count` (E3).

**Residue 1: `phase7_chrome.py`'s four Document-pane failures, fixed in the instrument.**
Section 5 solves the translucent note's shift over a band written down in points. The
summary's Colour row (HD-2) and the Canvas section's Dynamic Range and Blending rows (HD-2,
HD-16) moved the Appearance section down about 95 pt, so the band (y 615) lay across the
Background swatch, which a background change redraws. The opaque control's winning shift
then left 35 rows unexplained. The note row was found at the Appearance header's Reset (y
584) instead of under it, and read white ink. Every check that read the band failed, on
main as on C6a. The constants were re-measured from the script's own renders: `ABOVE_Y1`
500 → 595, which cuts through the Reset (584–606 pt), so the Reset is recognised and
excused; `BELOW_Y0` 615 → 660, the rows under the Background row (Timecode, Fit, Markers).
Markers alone is now too short to clear `SHIFT_MARGIN` in the opaque control: a band at 724
gave a runner-up of 23 rows against the 40 required. At 660 the translucent render's
runner-up is 100 rows and the control's 74. No app file changed for this.

**Residue 2: `graphic/tests/path.rs`'s timing budget, made robust.** R2, R4 and R5 ran their
render under the 250 ms preview budget as the engine's wall-clock call deadline. A load
average near 100 stretched R4's wall time past it, and the engine interrupted the call ("over
the 250 ms budget at frame 7"). That is a flaky gate, not a slow path. `timed` now runs the
call under a 10 s deadline (`HANG_MS`, which only a hang trips) and asserts the calling
thread's CPU time (`clock_gettime_nsec_np(CLOCK_THREAD_CPUTIME_ID)`; the engine is

(settings with a `writer`) is booked in `ExportEncoderLedger` from just before its
`Exporter.export` call to its finish — the queue's running job and every Export… progress
sheet's; a queued encoder job is admitted when nothing is booked or the booked costs and its
own fit a quarter of physical memory; a held job is passed over by a later admitted one and

        + "4K 25p, median of three runs per key and size, C6b; "

        + "Max, 96 GiB, one run per size (codec-export C5's fix pass); "

    /// run's figure and C6b's largest peak at the size, never lowered below a measured one.
    static let memory: [ExportEncoderKey: ExportEncoderFigure] = [
        ExportEncoderKey(preset: "av1", speed: .faster, bits: 10): ExportEncoderFigure(
            at1080: 1420640256, at2160: 4941070336,
            source: "1080p: " + run + "av1:faster; load 3.22–27.94 — 4K: " + c6aRun

        ExportEncoderKey(preset: "av1", speed: .balanced, bits: 10): ExportEncoderFigure(

            source: run + "av1:balanced; load 3.52–26.91 at 1080p, 8.35–22.85 at 4K"),
        ExportEncoderKey(preset: "av1", speed: .smaller, bits: 10): ExportEncoderFigure(

        ExportEncoderKey(preset: "av1_webm", speed: .faster, bits: 10): ExportEncoderFigure(

        ExportEncoderKey(preset: "av1_webm", speed: .balanced, bits: 10): ExportEncoderFigure(

            source: c6aRun + "av1_webm:smaller; load 10.14 at 1080p, 33.16 at 4K"),
        ExportEncoderKey(preset: "vp9_webm", speed: nil, bits: 8): ExportEncoderFigure(
            at1080: 397574144, at2160: 1130774528,
            source: "1080p: " + run + "vp9_webm:sdr; load 6.57–26.06 — 4K: " + c6aRun

        ExportEncoderKey(preset: "vp9_webm", speed: nil, bits: 10): ExportEncoderFigure(

            source: "1080p: " + run + "vp9_alpha_webm; load 7.40–22.15 — 4K: " + alphaRun
                + "vp9_alpha_webm; load 4.59"),

    /// Seconds. `perFrame` is the 250-frame export's median wall time less `setupSeconds`,

            perFrame: ExportEncoderFigure(

content.content: docs/manual-checks.md:384:- **Do:** 1. File ▸ Export… on a 4K project; pick **AV1 (MP4)** at each Speed, then **AV1 (WebM)**, **VP9 (WebM)** and H.264, and read the readout under the format each time. 2. cd /Users/kevingalligan/devel/framejob-codecs && cat >> designs/codec-export.md <<'EOF'

## C6b — 4K on every row and the final time constants

### Record

**Decision.** CX-18's amendment "**Amended by C6b**", recorded before the table edit
(`designs/spec/11-decisions/codec-export.md`): the time constants are the idle three-run
medians on real 4K footage, with a fixed start fitted from a long and a short batch.
`av1_webm` copies `av1`'s times (within 10 %). Each memory figure is the larger of the
earlier run's and C6b's peak. Nothing else in CX-18 moves: no change to the formula, the
ledger, the budget or `estimateText`.

**What landed.**
- `tools/proof/encoder_memory_measure.py` gained the AVFoundation rows, gif and apng as keys,
  size 1440 and `--media av|gh5|<path>`. It also takes `--fps`, `--seconds`, `--from`,
  `--runs`, `--label` and `--derive LONG SHORT`. Each row now records `estimated_seconds`,
  `settings_frames`, `expected_frames` and `written_frames`, the last counted by ffprobe from
  the file, or from an APNG's `fcTL` chunks. The JSON holds `uptime` at the start and end and
  the argv; outputs are deleted after their row; a medians table follows the per-run one. The
  defaults reproduce C6a's run.
- `app/Sources/ExportEncoderCosts.swift`: `run` is C6b's. `c6aRun` holds C6a's text verbatim
  for the memory figures C6a still wins. Every time constant and `setupSeconds` comes from the
  derive. Memory is raised where C6b's peak passed the earlier figure. The comments no longer
  say "provisional".
- `tools/proof/encoder_limit_proof.py` P0 requires every time source to name C6b and none to
  say "provisional".
- Spec §11 CX-18's amendment, its index rows and §7.8. The guide's export page: the readout's
  estimate sentence, the Speed table's measured times and sizes, the AV1 memory range and the
  estimate's limit. `docs/manual-checks.md` SE-20's per-sheet figure, 7.9 → 8.1 GB. The proof
  README's `encoder_memory_measure.py` paragraph.

**The machine.** Apple M2 Max (Mac14,6), 96 GiB, on AC, `powermode 0`, Release built from the
tree.
- **The first attempt stopped.** It began 2026-10-28 23:07. A's first run went through at a
  load of 2.22, but its APNG row hit the instrument bug below. Before A's re-run the 1-minute
  load stayed above 4 for the whole 15-minute wait (23:11–23:26; 8.02 at the end). The load
  came from Spotlight's `spotlightknowledged.updater` and `corespotlightd`, another session's
  Doctored Debug app, XProtect and a VM. Nothing was run past that point.
- **The second attempt** (2026-10-29) waited for a 1-minute load ≤ 4 before every batch, with
  no other Frame Job and no cargo, rustc, xcodebuild, swift-frontend or clang running. The
  `uptime` at each batch's start and end:

| Batch | Start | End |
|---|---|---|
| A (4K rows) | 1:39, load 3.74 4.43 4.56 | 1:42, 3.20 3.80 4.27 |
| B (long) | 1:42, 3.67 3.88 4.29 | 1:53, 21.48 23.14 15.35 |
| S (short) | 1:56, 3.22 13.95 12.98 | 2:00, 16.18 13.87 13.10 |
| V (validate) | 2:06, 3.90 8.95 11.09 | 2:08, 11.30 10.41 11.41 |

  The loads read during a batch, up to about 40, are the batch's own encoders: SVT-AV1 and
  libvpx run a thread per core, and the 1-minute average carries one export's threads into
  the next one's start. B's three runs of each key and size agree within 0.6–3.9 % (min to
  max), which no outside load would leave.

**The fixture.** The owner's GH5 borough-market clip, `tools/proof/media/log-samples/` (H.264
High 8-bit 3840 × 2160 25p, 55.21 s, gitignored), on a 25 fps canvas at each size, one clip
at 0 and its in/out range exported. For A, B and S that is 0–10 s (250 frames) or 0–2 s (50
frames). For V it is 20–50 s (750 frames).

**A — 4K on every AVFoundation and image row** (`work/encoder-memory/2026-10-29/c6b-4k-rows.json`,
one run each, 3840 × 2160, 10 s):

| Key | Δ RSS GiB | Seconds | Frames written / expected | s/frame | MB | Load |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| h264 | 0.27 | 3.008 | 250 / 250 | 0.01203 | 36.92 | 3.52 |
| hevc | 0.26 | 2.730 | 250 / 250 | 0.01092 | 18.61 | 3.88 |
| hevc_alpha | 0.26 | 5.092 | 250 / 250 | 0.02037 | 18.74 | 4.37 |
| hevc_10bit | 0.02 | 2.820 | 250 / 250 | 0.01128 | 18.73 | 4.02 |
| prores_422 | 0.18 | 1.074 | 250 / 250 | 0.00430 | 572.33 | 3.70 |
| prores_4444 | 0.59 | 1.782 | 250 / 250 | 0.00713 | 1424.17 | 4.04 |
| gif (12.5 fps) | 11.48 | 35.310 | 125 / 125 | 0.28248 | 498.19 | 3.80 |
| apng | 7.85 | 94.137 | 250 / 250 | 0.37655 | 2443.58 | 3.41 |

Every row finished with the right frame count, none near the 900 s bound, and no instance log
had a `Frame Job: ` line. `hevc_10bit`'s 0.02 GiB is its sampled peak barely above baseline,
as in A's first run (0.02). The AVFoundation rows book nothing in the ledger (CX-18 (2)).

**B — the long batch** (`c6b-long.json`, 3 runs × 7 keys × 2 sizes, 250 frames; 42/42 ok,
every file 250 frames). **S — the short batch** (`c6b-short.json`, the same at 50 frames;
42/42 ok, every file 50 frames). The medians, ranges, the derive's setup and per-frame
seconds, the median files and the largest Δ are the table in CX-18's amendment. The loads
during each key and size:

| Key | Size | B loads | S loads | B median est. (old table) | Old error |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| av1 faster | 1080p | 3.86–27.94 | 3.22–8.65 | 1 s | +58 % |
| av1 balanced | 1080p | 4.19–26.91 | 3.52–8.68 | 2 s | +52 % |
| av1 smaller | 1080p | 6.34–26.43 | 3.52–8.26 | 2 s | +66 % |
| av1_webm balanced | 1080p | 7.14–25.20 | 8.06–9.17 | 2 s | +51 % |
| vp9_webm SDR | 1080p | 6.57–26.06 | 8.46–14.14 | 2 s | +72 % |
| vp9_webm HLG | 1080p | 7.35–23.50 | 9.05–14.77 | 2 s | +78 % |
| vp9_alpha_webm | 1080p | 7.40–22.15 | 8.48–14.15 | 3 s | +62 % |
| av1 faster | 4K | 6.64–20.78 | 8.20–13.98 | 3 s | +58 % |
| av1 balanced | 4K | 9.29–22.85 | 8.35–13.26 | 7 s | +50 % |
| av1 smaller | 4K | 19.44–28.90 | 7.68–12.60 | 7 s | +65 % |
| av1_webm balanced | 4K | 24.43–32.50 | 8.26–13.56 | 5 s | +64 % |
| vp9_webm SDR | 4K | 29.91–39.50 | 8.32–12.71 | 5 s | +79 % |
| vp9_webm HLG | 4K | 23.05–32.01 | 8.57–11.81 | 8 s | +74 % |
| vp9_alpha_webm | 4K | 16.50–30.28 | 7.96–16.54 | 8 s | +70 % |

| vp9_alpha_webm | 4K | 16.50–30.28 | 7.96–16.54 | 8 s | +70 % |

The old (C6a) table's estimates were 50–79 % short of real footage: AV.mov at 640 × 360
scaled up is far easier to encode than camera footage. That gap is what C6b replaced.

**The derive** (`--derive c6b-long.json c6b-short.json`; n_L 250, n_S 50). The intercepts at
1080p and 4K:
- `av1` faster: 0.524 and 0.712 s, so setup 0.524.
- `av1` balanced: 0.738 and 1.261 s, so setup 0.738.
- `av1` smaller: 0.736 and 1.433 s, so setup 0.736.
- `av1_webm` balanced: 0.753 and 1.227 s (not used: it copies `av1`).
- `vp9_webm` SDR: 0.446 and 0.170 s, so setup 0, because the 4K intercept is under 0.5 s.
- `vp9_webm` HLG: 0.278 and −0.057 s, so setup 0.
- `vp9_alpha_webm`: 0.446 and 0.206 s, so setup 0.

The per-frame seconds and the literals are the table's. `av1_webm:balanced`'s medians were
−1.9 % (1080p) and −0.1 % (4K) of `av1:balanced`'s, inside the 10 % rule, so `av1_webm`'s
three time entries copy `av1`'s, and its Faster and Smaller were not run in B or S.

**Memory** (max of the earlier figure and C6b's largest Δ across B and S):
- **C6b won at both sizes:**
  - `av1` balanced: 2,386,313,216 and 8,030,453,760.
  - `av1` smaller: 2,613,837,824 and 8,696,889,344.
  - `av1_webm` balanced: 2,342,584,320 and 8,196,833,280.
- **C6b won at 1080p; the earlier figure kept 4K:**
  - `av1` faster: 1,420,640,256 (4K C6a's 4,941,070,336).
  - `vp9_webm` SDR: 397,574,144 (4K C6a's 1,130,774,528).
  - `vp9_alpha_webm`: 802,816,000 (4K C5's 2,326,249,472).
- **Unchanged under `c6aRun`:**
  - `vp9_webm` HLG, whose C6b peaks of 532,463,616 and 1,674,248,192 sit below C6a's.
  - `av1_webm` faster and smaller, which were not run.

The S batch's peaks are lower than B's (a 2 s export does not fill the lookahead), so every
C6b win came from B.

**The speed claims hold** at both sizes for `av1`:
- **Time:** Faster < Balanced < Smaller, at 2.380 < 4.175 < 5.792 s (1080p) and 7.127 < 13.971
  < 19.887 s (4K).
- **File size:** Smaller < Balanced < Faster, at 5.10 < 5.39 < 5.60 MB (1080p) and 14.61 <
  16.53 < 20.92 MB (4K).

The guide's Speed table now gives those measurements. CX-2's names stay. No issue was filed.

**V — the held-out check** (`c6b-validate.json`; 2560 × 1440, 20–50 s of the clip, 750
frames, one run; built with the new constants and never fed back into them). The estimate is
`export_status`'s `estimated_seconds`, and the tolerance is |elapsed − estimate| ≤ 25 % of
elapsed:

| Key | Elapsed s | Estimate s | Error | Δ GiB | MB | Load |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| av1:smaller | 28.171 | 27 | +4.2 % | 4.03 | 23.41 | 5.67 |
| av1_webm:faster | 9.699 | 10 | −3.1 % | 2.27 | 28.54 | 10.18 |
| vp9_webm:sdr | 30.306 | 34 | −12.2 % | 0.58 | 25.38 | 11.01 |
| vp9_alpha_webm | 33.493 | 38 | −13.5 % | 1.15 | 25.43 | 11.10 |

All four are within 25 %, every file had 750 frames, and no log had a `Frame Job: ` line.
VP9 is over-estimated by 12–14 % at 1440p. That fits its per-frame time growing slower than
the pixel count between 1080p and 4K, which the straight line through the two points does
not follow. Not re-tuned (out of scope).

**Findings.**
1. **The instrument: APNG's path and count, both fixed in `encoder_memory_measure.py`.** The
   app writes an APNG with PNG's UTI, so `out.apng` is written as `out.apng.png` (the
   destination rule appends the extension). The script now counts and deletes the done
   answer's `path`. Then ffprobe's APNG demuxer counted 218 packets in the 2.4 GB 4K file,
   whose `acTL` declares 250 frames, with 250 `fcTL` chunks to the end. A 960 × 540 APNG
   counted 250 in both. The demuxer stops near 2 GiB (218 × 9.8 MB ≈ 2.13 GB), so an APNG is
   now counted by its chunks, cross-checked against `acTL`. **Not an app defect; no issue.**
2. **A 4K GIF or APNG is heavy:** 11.48 GiB above baseline for a 4K GIF and 7.85 GiB for a 4K
   APNG, neither booked by the ledger (they are not writer rows). Both are custom sizes far
   above the presets' own (480 × 270 and 960 × 540). Recorded here, not filed: step 4 files a
   failed, timed-out, wrong-count or complaining row, and none was.
3. No A, B, S or V row failed, timed out or wrote the wrong count, and no instance log
   carried a `Frame Job: ` line. No issue was filed.

**Machine time.** The first attempt took about 20 min, 15 of them the wait. The second took
about 40 min to V's end (1:28–2:08), including two diagnostic APNG exports.

# C6b — implementation notes

Done. Every step of 03-spec-final.md ran. The first attempt (2026-10-28 23:07) stopped on the idle rule: the load stayed above 4 for the whole 15-minute wait, from Spotlight, another session's Doctored app, XProtect and a VM. On the owner's word the second attempt (2026-10-29 01:28–02:14) resumed and finished. The full record is `designs/codec-export.md`'s `## C6b`.

## What was done

- **`tools/proof/encoder_memory_measure.py`** follows the spec's Interfaces:
  - The new keys (`sized` on gif and apng), size 1440, and `--media/--fps/--seconds/--from/--runs/--label/--derive`.
  - `settings_frames`, `written_frames` (ffprobe `-count_packets`, after the timing, before deletion) and `expected_frames`, with a gap of more than 1 frame being the row's error.
  - `estimated_seconds` from one `export_status`, and `uptime` start and end plus the argv in the JSON.
  - Outputs deleted, a medians table, and `--derive` with the pre-C6b `frames` fallback and exit 2 on mixed or equal counts.
- **Batches**, each started at a 1-minute load ≤ 4 with no other Frame Job or build running:
  - A (8 rows), B (42) and S (42) all ok, with the right frame counts and no `Frame Job: ` lines.
  - V: 4/4 within 25 % (+4.2, −3.1, −12.2, −13.5 %).
- **Derive and step 5's rules.**
  - `av1_webm:balanced` came within 10 % of `av1:balanced` (−1.9 % at 1080p, −0.1 % at 4K), so `av1_webm`'s three time entries copy `av1`'s.
  - setupSeconds: `av1` 0.524 / 0.738 / 0.736; `vp9` rows 0, because their 4K intercepts are under 0.5 s.
  - Memory raised where C6b's peak was higher:
    - `av1` balanced and smaller, `av1_webm` balanced: both sizes.
    - `av1` faster, `vp9_webm` SDR, `vp9_alpha_webm`: 1080p only.
    - Kept: `vp9_webm` HLG, plus `av1_webm` faster and smaller (not run).
  - Speed claims hold at both sizes (time F < B < S, bytes S < B < F). No issue was filed.
- **`ExportEncoderCosts.swift`**:
  - `run` is C6b's, and `c6aRun` holds C6a's text verbatim.
  - Memory figures that C6a or C5 still win name `c6aRun` or `alphaRun`, size by size where the two sizes differ.
  - Every time source ends in `; C6b`, with no "provisional".
  - Comments updated. Types and functions unchanged.
- **P0** in `encoder_limit_proof.py` (and its docstring line).
- **Documents:** the CX-18 "Amended by C6b" paragraph with the medians table (written before the Swift edit); the 11-decisions README's two rows and the Lines cell; §7.8; the spec README's two cells; the `## C6b` record; the guide's lines 34, 89–91, 206 and 336; the proof README's paragraph with the flags, the fixture and the batch commands.

## Deviations and why

1. **APNG frame count.** `written_frames` for an APNG is its `fcTL` chunk count, cross-checked against `acTL`, not ffprobe's packet count.
   - ffprobe's APNG demuxer counted 218 of 250 frames in the 2.4 GB 4K file. Two diagnostic exports (a scratch script, scratchpad only) showed `acTL` = 250 and 250 `fcTL` chunks at 4K. At 960 × 540 ffprobe and the chunks both gave 250.
   - So this is an ffprobe limit near 2 GiB, not an app defect, and I filed no issue. Every other row uses ffprobe as specified.
2. **APNG path.** The script counts and deletes the done answer's `path`, because the app writes `out.apng` as `out.apng.png` (PNG's UTI).
3. **Re-runs of A.** A ran three times in all; the JSON holds the last run.
   - The first run (10-28) hit item 2.
   - The second (10-29, 01:31) hit item 1.
   - The third (01:39) is the recorded one.

   These were instrument fixes, not the GIF/APNG timeout case the spec says not to re-run.
4. **Date.** The batches ran on 2026-10-29, so the JSONs are under `work/encoder-memory/2026-10-29/` and `run` says 2026-10-29. C6a's `2026-10-28/memory.json` was only read.

## Files touched outside the Files list

- `docs/manual-checks.md`: SE-20's "about 7.9 GB each" (AV1 Smaller at 4K) became "about 8.1 GB each", because C6b raised that memory figure to 8,696,889,344 bytes. One figure only.

## For the orchestrator

- A 4K GIF used 11.48 GiB above baseline and a 4K APNG 7.85 GiB. The ledger books neither, since they are not writer rows. Both are custom sizes far above the presets' own (480 × 270 and 960 × 540).
- That memory is recorded in `## C6b` but not filed, because step 4's finding rule did not cover it. It may deserve a low-priority issue if the owner wants image rows in the ledger.
